title: Cloud Composer: managed Airflow and the cost of leaving it idle

videos.script: Every data platform has a pipeline that must run at three in the morning, and something has to start it. {{clock}} Airflow is the tool most teams reach for. A pipeline is a Python file, and Airflow runs its tasks in order, retries them, and remembers every run. {{dag}} Cloud Composer is Airflow run by Google. You give it a bucket of DAG files, and Google keeps the scheduler, the workers and the database running. {{parts}} There is no emulator for Composer. So you will install the real Airflow on your laptop and run Quitanda's pipeline with it, Spark job included. {{laptop}} Running is the word to hold on to. An environment cannot be paused. The smallest one costs over five hundred dollars a month, whether it works one hour a night or twenty. {{bill}} Then the same pipeline without Airflow: a workflow, started by Cloud Scheduler, which cost nothing while they wait. {{workflows}} And the question Airflow answers that they cannot: which night is this run for? {{end}}
